newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares fall at bourse open, meet late IBIS.
newsitem.headline: German shares fall at bourse open, meet late IBIS.

text.p: German shares opened bourse trade lower on Thursday as they caught up with losses made in late computer trade on Wednesday, when the IBIS DAX fell following a surprise interest rate rise in Britain.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares was down 13.98 points, or 0.52 percent, at 2,664.75 by 1020 GMT.

The U.K. rate announcement came just before the close of floor dealings and the market did not have time to digest the news, which was taken as a signal that there would probably be no further German interest rate cuts.
But the German bond market, which had fallen on the UK rate hike, recovered on Thursday, providing some support to the share market.
Overall, dealers said the market tone was mixed, following a lower close on Wall Street and a weaker dollar against the mark, with attention focussed on a few individual stocks.
They said the market would be reticent ahead of important U.S. data due out later in the day and on Friday.
Meanwhile the banking sector was the main centre of attention as nine month results were released.

Dresdner Bank had risen in IBIS dealings, after it said its operating profits rose 29.7 percent to 1.89 billion marks for the first nine months of the year. But the stock was unchanged in floor trade at 41 marks, holding against the market trend.
Shares in business software compnay SAP AG fell on continued worries about firm, formerly the market's favourite, after it issued a profit warning last week.
